To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the dynamic model of smart material robots can be obtained by using the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory; (2) model free control is a promising method for smart material robots; (3) tracking control of smart material robot can be achieved by employing singular perturbations.

(1) The dynamic modelling and control methods of single-link smart material manipulators were investigated; (2) Model-free control of single-link smart materials robots is proposed; (3) Singular perturbation based control method is proposed to achieve direct control of link deformation.

1) the dynamic modelling and control problem of smart material flexible robots are solved; 2) the model free control problem of smart materials robots are investigated, and 3) the tracking problem of smart materials flexible robots are solved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modelling and control of a single link flexible robot with a shape memory alloy (SMA) actuator.
the modelling and control of flexible manipulators with smart material actuators.
the modelling and control of flexible robots, and the application of smart materials in robotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
smart material robots are very interesting to study and have great potential to be used in many applications.
the smart materials can be used to improve the performance of the flexible manipulator, and to reduce the control complexity.
the smart material robots have the potential to be the next generation robots.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by using the non model based controllers and the singular perturbation techniques, the dynamic model is not necessary for control design and thus the dynamic modelling and control design for smart material robots become much simpler.
the presented methods can be used to design smart material robots that have better control performances and higher stability robustness.
the dynamic modelling of smart material flexible robots is presented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the smart material robots can be controlled without knowing the dynamic model of the system.
, through the use of smart materials, the dynamic model and the control of flexible manipulators can be simplified.
smart material actuators can be used to control flexible manipulators without knowing the dynamic model of the system.
